search_log: Searched Penguin Random House and Paula Hawkins sources for an authorized excerpt or structural description; opened the US and UK publisher pages.
Searched “The Girl on the Train” with “three narrators,” “point of view,” and “first-person narrators”; opened the Washington Post review, GradeSaver analysis, and the author’s Goodreads notes.
Searched scholarly and university sources for first-person narration; opened full University of Helsinki and Tribhuvan University theses.

The US Penguin Random House page confirmed multiple narrators through review material but its interactive Read Sample text was not exposed; the UK publisher page supplied an explicit first-person description.
Targeted searches found no credible evidence of sustained second- or third-person base sections.
person_note: The quote set repeatedly exposes participating narration through “I,” “me,” and “my,” while the few second-person forms are generic or occur in dialogue. Scholarly analysis and multiple explicit reviews establish that Rachel, Megan, and Anna are all first-person narrators, so their alternation is among narrators rather than grammatical persons and the book remains FIRST. The clipped q03484 and locally unmarked passages do not contradict that structure. No material uncertainty remains beyond the quotes’ lack of narrator-name headings. Source audit: the author's Goodreads annotation is contextual Tier C evidence rather than a Tier A excerpt; explicit scholarly and review descriptions support FIRST independently.
